main_text.l: norum igitur Baritus. quem & Romani inferiores af- sumpsêre, nec vno loco ijs tribuit, & describit Ammia-nus. Vt in concione Constantij Imp. ad milites: Vt nec oculorum vestrorum vibratæ lucis ardorem, nec baritus sonum perferant primum. Alibi: Et Romani quidem voce vndique Martiâ concinentes, à minore solitâ ad maiorem protolli, quam gentilitate appellant Baritum. Vbi describitur in parte etiam Baritus: clariusque eidem, de Germanis ipsis: Gesturientes Baritum ciere vel maximum, qui clamor ipso feruore certaminũ àtenui susurro exoriens, paullatímque adolescens, ritu extollitur fluctuum cautibus illisorum. Hic Baritus igitur, qui in Festo etiam Barbaricum dictus: Barbaricum appellatur clamor exercitus, quòd eo genere barbari vtantur. At Romani non clamore solum vsi, sed strepitu etiam & concussione armorum.

Polybius in pugnâ Reguli cum Xantippo: κατὰ τὰ παρ' αὐτοῖς ἐθη σωεψόφησαν τοῖς ὅπλοις καὶ συωαλαλάξοντες ὥρμησαν ἐπὶ τὰς πολεμίας: Ex more ijs consueto armis concrepuerunt, & vnà clamantes inuaserunt hostem.

Idem in pugnâ Scipionis cum Annibale: Οἱ ῥωμαῖοι κα- τὰ τὰ πάτρια συναλαλάξαντες καὶ συμψοφήσαντες τῇς ξίφεσι τὰς ἀσπίδας, ἐπέσχεθον τοῖς ἐναντίοις: Romani, iuxta morem patrium, clamore sublato, & gladijs adscuta concrepantes, inuaserunt oppositos.

Dio Cassius in pugnâ Pompeij nocturnâ cum Mithirdate: πρῶτον μὲν οἱ σαλπιγκταὶ πάντες ἅμα τὸ πολεμικὸν ὑπὸ σωθήματος ἐδόησαν. ἐπειτα δ' οἱ τε ἐφεστῶτες καὶ ὁ λοιπὸς ὄχλος πᾶς ἐπηλάλαξε. καὶ οἱ μὲν τὰ δόρατα πρὸς τὰς ἀσπίδας, οἱ δὲ καὶ λίθος πρὸς τὰ χαλκᾶ σκευὴ προσεπέιρεσαν: Primum tubicines omnes ex composito* simul bellicum cecinerunt: tum milites

page.notes: The text in the right margin is partly cramped; "Lib. xxxvii." and the Greek of the Dio passage are read with some doubt. The Greek lines are copied from a cursive print and may contain letters I could not confirm; no [?] is placed on them because I could not reliably isolate individual words. The asterisk after "composito" refers to the margin note "Quod nō sic solet, vt ante monui." The "&" mark at the foot of the page belongs to the same passage and is not a separate note. Long s is written as s throughout.
